title: Usage Attribution Matrix + SLO UI notes
body:
Summary:
This is a working doc for a combined "usage attribution matrix" and SLO visualization concept for the Console's per-key / per-route usage pages. Goal: make it trivial for an engineer or CS rep to answer two questions quickly: 1) Where are my tokens being consumed (by key, route, model, and feature)? 2) Are we close to SLOs and quota limits, and what are the remediation paths?

Context / problem notes:
- Feedback from pilot customers: current per-key breakdowns show raw token counts but don’t explain where cost is coming from (e.g., streaming vs non-streaming, reranking reruns, embeddings batch spikes).
- Support and sales frequently need a single view that attributes costs to features (chat, embeddings, search rerank) so they can recommend concrete config changes (e.g., enable prefix cache, lower top_p, move to quantized model).
- Existing console graphs are separate (usage graph, quotas panel, route list). Users have to click 3 places to diagnose a single incident.

Proposal (high level):
- Introduce an "Attribution Matrix" table at the top of the per-key page. Rows: Key (or Route if route-view). Columns: Model variant, Feature bucket (generation, streaming, embeddings, rerank), Avg tokens per request, 24h tokens, 7d tokens, Est cost (USD), % of key total, Recent error rate.
- Add a small SLO row under the matrix showing SLOs (latency p95, availability) and quota burn rate with timeline sparkline. Color-coded badges (green/amber/red).
- Allow an interactive "slice" control: choose dimension to pivot the matrix by (model, route, feature, region, user-agent). This control is lightweight (chip list) and persists per-user.

Wireframe / micro-interactions (notes for design):
1) Top bar: Key selector (dropdown) + timeframe quick chips (24h, 7d, 30d) + export button (CSV / JSON).
2) Attribution Matrix: compact table with inline bar visual for % of key total. Hover on a cell shows mini breakdown (e.g., for Streaming: show % from partial responses, prefix cache hit rate). Clicking a row opens a right rail with per-route timeline and sample requests.
3) SLO row: shows numeric SLOs + small trend sparkline and projected burn (based on 7d average). If projected burn crosses quota within X days, show a callout with recommended actions (reduce max_tokens, enable batching for embeddings, switch route to cheaper model).
4) Route-level drill: clicking any Feature bucket drills into per-route view scaffolded with top offending requests by token cost and the exact prompt (redacted). Provide quick action buttons: create support ticket, open canary rollout, or apply temporary rate-limiting rule.
5) Lightweight annotations: allow users to pin a note to a particular time window (e.g., "spike due to import job from client XYZ"). Pins show up in the timeline and in the right-rail context.

Data model considerations (engineering notes):
- Attribution requires join of routing table + per-request metadata (model, stream flag, route id, tool calls) + billing tokens. We expect eventual consistency: accept a ~1h latency on full attribution rebuild.
- Need to surface uncertainty % for estimated cost lines (e.g., "+/- 3% due to deduped streaming tokens").
- Caching: pre-aggregate daily matrices per key for 7d/30d queries; compute real-time deltas for last 4 hours.

Backlog / priority (MVP -> later):
MVP (must-have for next sprint):
- Attribution Matrix table: Feature buckets (generation | streaming | embeddings | rerank), 24h & 7d tokens, % of key total, est cost column.
- Timeframe chips and key selector.
- Simple SLO row with p95 latency and quota burn % + color badge.
- CSV export for matrix.

Near-term (post-MVP):
- Right-rail drill with redacted example requests + quick actions (create ticket / apply temporary throttle).
- Slice control pivot by model/route/region.
- Pin/annotation UX and timeline integration.

Later / wishlist:
- Forecasting: projected quota exhaustion calculator with hypothetical slider (what if avg changes by +25%?).
- Automated recommendations engine (match usage fingerprints to config templates: "enable batching", "lower response size") and one-click apply to dedicated pools.
- Multi-key cohort view for org-level attribution (support-driven).

Acceptance criteria (for MVP):
- A user can open a key page and see an attribution table that explains >=80% of token burn by feature bucket for the last 24h.
- SLO row correctly reflects latest p95 latency within 5% of backend metric and shows color state (green/amber/red) computed by thresholds in the config.
- Exported CSV matches on-screen totals for 24h tokens and USD estimate.
- Page loads in <2s for keys with up to 1M tokens/day (use pre-aggregates).

Open questions / tradeoffs to discuss at grooming:
- Feature bucketing rules: how granular do we want (should "streaming partials" be its own bucket or part of generation?).
- Privacy: how much prompt content can we store/display in redacted examples? Legal wants default redaction and opt-in for full text.
- UI complexity: prefer progressive disclosure (matrix -> drill) vs a denser single-page dashboard. Customer interviews indicate a bias toward progressive disclosure.
- SLA implications: do we show projected quota exhaustion to end users or only to admin roles?

Example mock data (for prototypes):
Key: api-key-abc123
Timeframe: last 24h
Attribution Matrix rows (top 4):
- Generation | model: redwood-gen-xl | avg tokens/req: 450 | 24h tokens: 1,250,000 | est cost: $312.50 | % of key: 62% | err rate: 0.5%
- Streaming (chat) | model: redwood-chat-m | avg tokens/req: 120 | 24h tokens: 300,000 | est cost: $45.00 | % of key: 15% | err rate: 1.2%
- Embeddings (batch) | model: redwood-embed-s | avg tokens/req: 5 | 24h tokens: 200,000 | est cost: $20.00 | % of key: 10% | err rate: 0.0%
- Rerank (search) | model: redwood-rerank | avg tokens/req: 30 | 24h tokens: 100,000 | est cost: $25.00 | % of key: 5% | err rate: 0.2%
(Other/unattributed: 8%)

Design annotations:
- Small inline help (i) for each column explaining "est cost" assumptions (unit price, rounding, exclusions).
- Hover tooltip for "% of key" should show absolute token numbers and the formula used.
- Color scale for est cost: small gradient from light to dark orange; cap max hex to ensure high-contrast for accessibility.

Engineering follow-ups / tickets to create:
- Build aggregation job: daily_key_attribution (owner: infra-telemetry).
- Frontend: matrix component + pivot control (owner: console-ui).
- Backend: SLO projection endpoint + quota projection (owner: serving-runtime).

Notes from preliminary customer calls (to include in next iteration):
- CS at AcmeCorp asked for ability to save a "diagnostic snapshot" and attach to a support ticket (include pinned timeline and top 3 offending requests).
- Security team: must ensure per-request samples are redacted by default and that redaction can be audited.

Next steps / meeting items:
- Sync with infra-telemetry on feasibility and cost estimates (action: Ethan to schedule).
- Design hi-fi for matrix and right-rail (action: Lydia to prototype by 2025-02-25).
- Legal/security review for redaction rules (action: Amira to draft policy).

Appendix: short glossary for non-product folks:
- Attribution matrix: an aggregated table that maps tokens and cost back to features and models so teams can act on cost drivers.
- Feature bucket: high-level classification of request types (generation, streaming, embeddings, rerank).
- Prefix cache: runtime optimization that reduces tokens billed for repeated initial prompts.

Timestamped notes (internal):
- 2025-02-12 initial draft by Priya; included customer quotes from 2025-02-10 call.
- 2025-02-18 added example mock data after design sync.
- 2025-03-04 updated acceptance criteria and added export requirement per support ask.
